subject: Appeal: temporary sandbox credit while procurement verifies vendor details
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@novamed.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary sandbox credit while procurement verifies vendor details

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time with the demo yesterday — the NovaMed team had some great questions and I want to keep momentum while procurement finishes their validation. I understand your AP/Procurement folks are reconciling a vendor registration item that should clear within a few business days.

To avoid losing the progress from the demo, would a short-term protective credit help? I can propose a temporary sandbox uplift (no long-term billing, just a time-limited token grant) while your procurement/legal teams complete the review.

What I need from you to proceed:
- Confirmation that procurement is actively validating (one-line from procurement or legal is fine)
- A contact@procurement address I can route the formal acknowledgement to (I cc'd the Procurement Team address I have on file)

I attached the sandbox usage report from your demo (sandbox-usage-report.csv) and a quick draft PO (NovaMed_PO_Draft.pdf) that legal can use to speed things up. If you prefer, we can provide a 72-hour uplift to keep the environment live and share a short DocuSign link for acknowledgement instead of a PO.

Proposed guardrails:
- 72-hour credit for up to 25,000 generation tokens (instrumented as "sponsored-sandbox" so we can revert if needed)
- No automatic conversion to paid usage — we'll only bill if a PO/contract is returned and signed
- We require a written note from procurement/finance acknowledging the review is in progress before we provision

If that sounds reasonable, reply here and I’ll escalate for a quick internal approval.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: sandbox-usage-report.csv (CSV, 12KB)
Attachment: NovaMed_PO_Draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary sandbox credit while procurement verifies vendor details

Hi Naomi,

Appreciate the follow-up. Procurement is on it — legal is looking at the vendor form and a couple of compliance questions came up (standard stuff about data residency and the onboarding questionnaire). Not expected to be a long delay but could take 3–5 business days.

The Procurement Team above is the best contact for official confirmation. If you can provide a short 72-hour uplift it would help us run a weekend integration pass. Would the uplift require a signed PO in advance? If so, can we sign a minimal acknowledgement instead?

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Product Operations, NovaMed
liam@novamed.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@novamed.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary sandbox credit while procurement verifies vendor details

Thanks Liam — copying procurement directly to keep everything documented.

Procurement/Finance team,

We can provide a time-limited uplift to NovaMed to preserve their integration work while your review completes. Our standard short-form process for these cases is:

- Customer signs a short acknowledgement (one paragraph) confirming procurement is validating in good faith and that the uplift is temporary
- Redwood provisions a 72-hour sandbox credit (up to 25k tokens under tag "sponsored-sandbox")
- Customer agrees that if a PO/contract is returned within that window, Redwood will proceed per normal invoicing; otherwise the uplift expires with no charge

I’ve attached a one-line acknowledgement template and the draft PO to speed things up. Camila and David from my team are cc'd for internal provisioning/approval.

If procurement can reply with a one-line email like:
"Procurement confirms vendor registration/validation is in progress and requests a time-limited sandbox uplift for NovaMed (Liam O'Reilly)."

— we’ll provision within the hour after internal sign-off. Alternatively, Liam, if procurement prefers DocuSign, we can send a DocuSign Acknowledgement link instead (link included in related links).

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Reilly <liam@novamed.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Temporary sandbox credit while procurement verifies vendor details

Naomi — I authorize a 72-hour sandbox uplift for NovaMed with the following internal controls:

1) Tag the provision as "sponsored-sandbox/DEAL-7832" in billing so it is auditable.
2) Limit the uplift to 25,000 generation tokens and disable any auto-conversion to a paid plan.
3) Require the one-line procurement acknowledgement in the thread (or signed DocuSign) before provisioning.
4) If no PO/contract is received within the 72 hours, the uplift will be auto-expired and we will archive the request under SALE-7832 for record-keeping.

Naomi — please provision once procurement confirms in-thread. David, please enable the token cap and tagging when Naomi asks provisioning.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Manager, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
